roadmap.goal: ADO #6354 'Updates that change nothing skip the forecast'. Slice 01 (ships alone): a periodic or event-triggered forecast whose inputs match the fingerprint recorded by the Portfolio's last completed forecast runs no simulation; the round's summary line ends ' | forecast=skipped after {N}ms (inputs unchanged)', a Forecast row marked skipped lands in the refresh log, and Refresh History shows the skip and keeps its duration figures to computed runs. The fingerprint is a pure value over what the simulation is handed (instance day included), stored on the Portfolio and written only by set-based CAS / forget statements; failure, cancel, an unfingerprintable input, any of the six buttons and every app start make the next forecast compute. Slice 02: a skip stamps the in-scope Features' forecasts confirmed now. Done when all 89 pending DISTILL tests are un-skipped and green, every active guard stays green, no `__SCAFFOLD__` of this Story remains, `dotnet build` has zero warnings, the filtered `dotnet test` is green, and `pnpm test` and `pnpm build` are clean. Docs, screenshots, release notes and mutation runs belong to finalization and are NOT steps here.
roadmap.paradigm_note: The Hypothesis + state-delta unit mandate from nw-roadmap does not apply, deliberately: the backend is C# .NET 10 with NUnit 4 + Moq and no property-testing library (no FsCheck/CsCheck), the frontend is Vitest + React Testing Library without fast-check. DISTILL authored every acceptance and unit scenario, example-based, with finite axes as `[TestCase]` / `[TestCaseSource]` (the 13 input changes, the 6 presses, the 20 one-member-changed and 5 too-sensitive fingerprint cases). RED is removing `[Ignore(Pending)]` / `it.skip` and watching the test fail on its assertion or on the `__SCAFFOLD__` NotImplementedException, as distill/red-classification.md records; GREEN is production code. Unit tests DISTILL left to DELIVER (ForecastUpdaterTest, ForecastServiceTest, five controller tests, RefreshLogDto mapping, seeder, golden value, cross-provider fingerprint equality) are written with the code in the step that needs them. Contract shapes per component are the feature-delta's 'Contract shapes (crafter assertions)' table.
exit_gates: End of every backend step: `dotnet build` zero warnings; the touched test classes green; the filtered `dotnet test --filter "TestCategory!=Integration&TestCategory!=JiraIntegration&TestCategory!=LinearIntegration&TestCategory!=AdoIntegration&TestCategory!=ServiceNowIntegration"` green (environmental signatures per CLAUDE.md are not regressions). Docker must be running: the filtered suite includes the Postgres container cases (SharedPostgresContainer), and without Docker they fail rather than skip.

End of the frontend step: `pnpm test` green and `pnpm build` clean with zero warnings (prebuild runs `biome check --write`; run `pnpm exec biome check ./src` read-only first and mind the docs-symlink hazard).

No push before the button-forget step (01-08) and the start-up-forget step (01-09) are green: until both land, an 'Update forecast' press or the first round after a start could skip. Phase 01 is committed step by step locally and pushed once, at its end.

End of phase 01 (releasable alone): full filtered backend suite (Docker running) and full `pnpm test` + `pnpm build` green; ordered migration build pass done and the throwaway SQLite start's log has no `PendingModelChanges`; the generated migration files on BOTH providers (Lighthouse.Migrations.Sqlite and Lighthouse.Migrations.Postgres) carry `defaultValue: false` for `RefreshLogs.Skipped`, and LighthouseAppContext carries no HasDefaultValue for it; time each of the five `Slice01*` acceptance classes, `ForecastInputFingerprintTest`, `ForecastInputFingerprintAcrossProvidersTests`, `ForecastUpdaterTest`, `ForecastConfirmationRepositoryRelationalTest` and `RefreshLogSkippedColumnMigrationTests` against the 34 s per-class budget (warn-only in CI: speed up, or allowlist with a reason and a ceiling >= 2.1x CI time); the only `__SCAFFOLD__` left is `ConfirmForecastsAsOf`, called by nothing; the push touches Program.cs, so CI runs every live-connector category: budget the full run plus one flake re-run and say so when pushing; dogfood reading on the dev instance (:5169): a quiet round logs the skip and a skip costs at most a third of a computed run of the same Portfolio (else DDD-2's lighter read is owed, not built here).

End of phase 02: full filtered backend suite green (Docker running), ForecastUpdaterTest's stamp cases included; `Slice02ConfirmedNowScenarios` and `ForecastUpdaterTest` timed against the 34 s budget; `grep -rn "__SCAFFOLD__" Lighthouse.Backend/Lighthouse.Backend` lists nothing of this Story.

user_decisions: MD-1 - Skip rule is a fingerprint of everything a Portfolio's forecast reads; skip when it matches the last run's (FetchFingerprint pattern).
MD-2 - Manual 'Update forecast' and refresh buttons bypass the skip; only background and automatic rounds may skip.
MD-3 - A skipped run stamps the forecasts confirmed now; the summary line says the forecast was skipped.
MD-4 - Coalescing back-to-back Team refreshes' forecasts is a follow-up, out of scope.
MD-5 - Today's date (the instance day) is a fingerprint member, so the first refresh of each day forecasts.
MD-6 - Every refresh a user starts forecasts (both 'update forecast' buttons, Team/Portfolio refresh, refresh-all), as amended by MD-10.
MD-7 - A skipped forecast keeps its own refresh-log row, marked skipped; Refresh History duration figures count computed runs only.
MD-8 - Task Manager unchanged: a skipped forecast's row appears and leaves as today, only faster.

MD-9 - Refresh History: Last Run reads 'skipped (nothing changed)', line 'Skipped (nothing changed): N of the last M runs', durations over computed runs, gaps at skips; spinner and 'Could not load refresh history.' unchanged.
MD-10 - (autonomous, revisit) 'Update forecast' guarantees a recompute; the four refresh buttons forget best-effort (recompute unless a forecast of that Portfolio ran in between).
MD-11 - (autonomous, revisit) Avg, Min and Max Duration show '—' when every run of a Forecast entity was skipped.
MD-12 - (autonomous, revisit) Last Run of a skip reads '<time> · skipped (nothing changed)', with ' · ' as separator.
MD-13 - (autonomous, revisit) Every app start forgets every Portfolio's fingerprint, so the first forecast after a start computes.
out_of_scope: Task Manager changes (MD-8); coalescing back-to-back forecasts (MD-4); seeding the simulation; partial forecasts; settings saves triggering a forecast themselves.
DDD-2's lighter read (Features without histograms) unless the phase-01 dogfood reading trips its trigger; then it is a follow-up, not a silent addition.

Usage-data event (N/A per DEVOPS: a skip is not a user action); Lighthouse-Clients (N/A, DDD-12 gate cleared, no version bump); website (N/A per DISCUSS, finalize greps); RBAC (N/A, no guard changes); new E2E (none, existing coverage is the sanity check).

Finalize items: docs/settings/taskmanager.md (MD-10 sentence: 'Update forecast always recomputes; a refresh you start recomputes unless a forecast of that Portfolio ran in between') and docs/settings/systeminfo.md (skip marker, count line, durations, dash); settings/systeminfo.png via the @screenshot run and settings/RefreshHistory.png by hand; ARCHITECTURE.md if the forecast trigger concept reads differently; Stryker.NET and StrykerJS on frozen code per the DEVOPS mutation scope (>= 80 %); release notes tag (maintainer); ADO state transitions.

steps.implementation_notes: EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: schema and wiring, verified by example migration and mapping tests. Pre-apply docs/ci-learnings.md. Do NOT write HasDefaultValue(false) in LighthouseAppContext: EF warns that false is the CLR sentinel for bool (it could never tell 'not set' from 'false'), and TreatWarningsAsErrors turns that into a red build. EF already emits `defaultValue: false` when it adds a non-nullable bool column to an existing table, so the default lives in the generated migration only; check both generated files for it. Never `dotnet ef migrations add`: `dotnet restore && dotnet build` the solution, then `pwsh Lighthouse.Backend/Create-Migration.ps1 -MigrationName <Name>`. Ordered build pass before calling it done: `dotnet build --no-incremental` Lighthouse.Migrations.Sqlite, then Lighthouse.Migrations.Postgres, then the solution, then a throwaway SQLite start grepped for PendingModelChanges. Postgres case through SharedPostgresContainer, fresh database per case (Docker running). Commit via des-commit, `--owned-paths` written once with every path. `feat(forecast): ...`.

steps.implementation_notes: EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: behaviour-preserving refactor; the existing suite is the guard. PORT SHAPE DECISION: change the one method (day in, outcome out) and update every caller in this commit. Rejected: (a) a second port method used only by ForecastUpdater - the two decorators and ForecastService must implement it anyway, every mock without a setup for it answers a null outcome (the same fixture sweep), and every existing Verify on the old method breaks silently the moment the updater stops calling it (`Times.Never` in PortfolioUpdaterTest would pass for the wrong reason; the `Times.Once` ones would go red), while leaving a near-duplicate method on the port; as an overload it would also trip S4136 (error-severity) in every implementing file.
